title: Evaluation of the Benefits of SmED-Patient in the Emergency Department
summary:
The "Structured Initial Medical Evaluation in Germany" (SmED) is a tool for assessing medical emergencies and acute complaints and their management. It is available in various versions, including one for professionals in contact with patients (SmED-Contakt+) and another that can be used by patients themselves (SmED-Patient).
This study examines the appropriateness and safety of SmED-Patient recommendations for acute complaints of patients in the emergency department and whether its use and the information obtained from it are beneficial for both patients and medical staff in the emergency department. The use of SmED-Patient could contribute to a needs-based and patient-centered care approach.
conditions: The entirety of emergency department patients is included. No specific diseases are examined.

interventions.name: Assessment of the patients using SmED-Contact+ by the study staff and self-assessment of the patients using SmED-Patient, in randomised order of the SmED assessments.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Independent presentation in one of the participating emergency departments (self-referral)
Feasibility of SmED patient (sufficient German or English language skills, verbal communication possible, sufficient cognition, etc.)
Exclusion criteria:
Minor
Admission or medical transport to the emergency department
Urgent medical care
Lack of capacity to consent
Insufficient knowledge of the German or English language
Legal guardianship
